meta.title: Design review: product page and cart (mobile web)
meta.scope: Product detail and cart screens of a fashion retailer, from two screenshots.

coverage.limitation: No navigation, category or search screens were supplied.

executive_summary.verdict: The product page presents the item well, but it withholds delivery cost and returns information until the cart and then defers shipping to a later step, which works against the goal of reducing abandonment. The size selector gives no guidance, and the cart quantity controls are small for touch.
strengths: Large, well-cropped product imagery leads the page and the price is clearly legible.
The cart shows a thumbnail, size and colour for each line, which lets users confirm what they chose.

findings.title: Shipping cost is not shown until after the cart

evidence.region: area under the price and above the size chips
evidence.observation: No delivery cost, delivery time or returns information appears anywhere on the product page.
The summary shows 'Shipping: calculated at next step' and a subtotal only, so the total cost is unknown.

findings.impact: Shoppers learn the full cost late, and unexpected delivery charges are a common reason to abandon a cart.
findings.recommendation: Show a delivery cost threshold and returns line on the product page (for example 'Free delivery over $50, free returns') and display an estimated shipping value in the cart summary.
findings.rationale: Revealing cost earlier removes uncertainty at the moment of decision, which supports the abandonment goal; confidence is medium because the screenshots may omit content below the fold.

findings.title: Add to bag looks active before a size is chosen, with no prompt

evidence.region: size chips and Add to bag button
evidence.observation: All size chips are unselected, no helper text asks the user to choose, and the Add to bag button is in its normal filled style.

findings.impact: If the button fails or errors without a size, users meet a dead end at the key conversion step; if it silently picks a size, they may receive the wrong one.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Select a size' prompt above the chips and either label the button 'Select size' until chosen or scroll to and highlight the chips on tap.
findings.rationale: Telling users what is needed before the action prevents the error path entirely; the behaviour on tap is inferred because a static screenshot cannot show it.

findings.title: Cart quantity buttons are small touch targets

evidence.region: quantity stepper on each line item
evidence.observation: The minus and plus buttons are drawn as small outlined squares close together beside the quantity number.
evidence.measurement: approx. 28x28 px each, estimated from screenshot

findings.impact: Mis-taps on a stepper next to a remove action can change or delete the wrong line on a phone.
findings.recommendation: Enlarge each stepper button to at least 44x44 px of touch area, with 8px or more between them, and keep the visual size if needed by padding the hit area.
findings.rationale: Finger-sized targets reduce accidental edits on the most frequently used cart control; measurements need confirming on the real layout.

findings.title: Add to bag and Checkout buttons appear to use two different greens

evidence.observation: The button is a mid green.
The button is a visibly darker green with a different corner radius.

findings.impact: Two primary-button styles for the same role make the system feel inconsistent and complicate maintenance.
findings.recommendation: Use one primary button token for both and confirm in the source files which value is intended.
findings.rationale: Shared tokens keep primary actions recognisable across pages; confidence is limited because compression may shift the colours in the screenshots.

assumptions: The screenshots show the complete page content; nothing relevant sits below the captured area.
open_questions: Is delivery cost known before an address is entered? If not, the estimate in the cart may need a postcode field.
What happens on tapping Add to bag without a size?

annotations.label: No size prompt before Add to bag

concepts.title: Delivery and returns strip
concepts.description: Add a compact strip under the price with delivery threshold and returns policy, linked to a short details sheet, and mirror an estimated shipping line in the cart summary.
concepts.tradeoffs: Takes vertical space on the product page and requires the policy to be kept in sync with operations.
concepts.expected_impact: Fewer shoppers reaching checkout surprised by costs, which can be measured as cart-to-checkout continuation.

limitations: Static screenshots only: tap behaviour, validation and animation were not observed.
Dimension scores reflect two screens and should not be read as a store-wide judgment.
